title: Fire Marshal operational permits for a glass studio: hot work, compressed gases and oxygen, LP-gas, industrial ovens, places of assembly, open flames and tents
question: Which Albemarle County Fire Rescue (Fire Marshal's Office) permits does a glass studio need for its gas furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches, oxygen and propane, and for classes, demonstrations and events, how do I apply, what do they cost, and how do inspections and appeals work?
office: Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Community Risk & Resilience section (the Fire Marshal's Office; the fire official under the Statewide Fire Prevention Code)
summary: Albemarle County enforces the Virginia Statewide Fire Prevention Code (SFPC, 13VAC5-52, the 2021 edition effective January 18, 2024) through Fire Rescue's Community Risk & Resilience section, and its Fire Marshal fee schedule (effective January 19, 2022) fills in SFPC Table 107.2 to say which operational permits the County requires and what they cost. For a hot glass studio the likely set is: hot work (fixed-site equipment such as a glory hole or torch bench, and public demonstrations), compressed gas once oxygen exceeds 504 cubic feet or a flammable gas 200 cubic feet, LP-gas for any propane storage and use outside a home, industrial ovens for fuel-fired furnaces and kilns regulated by IFC Chapter 30, a place of assembly permit if more than 50 people gather for classes, demonstrations or events, open flames and candles if a dining area uses them, and a tent permit for an outdoor event tent over 900 square feet. Most permits are $200 a year per location (cutting and welding $100 per event); the facility inspection before issuance is free for the first two hours and $100 an hour after; re-inspections are $100 when violations are not corrected. Apply on the Fire Prevention Permit Application (General) web form; permits must be kept on the premises and renew annually by the inspection anniversary. Decisions can be appealed to the local Board of Fire Prevention Code Appeals within 14 calendar days ($350 application fee on the County schedule), then to the State Building Code Technical Review Board.

legal_basis.quote: The Fire Prevention Code shall prescribe regulations to be complied with for the protection of life and property from the hazards of fire or explosion and for the handling, storage, sale, and use of fireworks, explosives, or blasting agents, and shall provide for the administration and enforcement of such regulations.

Any local government may enforce the Fire Prevention Code in its entirety or with respect only to those provisions of the Fire Prevention Code relating to open burning, fire lanes, fireworks, and hazardous materials.
Appeals concerning the application of the Code by the local enforcing agency shall first lie to a local board of appeals and then to the State Building Code Technical Review Board.
A schedule of such costs shall be adopted by the local governing body in a local ordinance.

Any such violation shall be deemed a Class 1 misdemeanor, and any owner, or any other person, firm, or corporation convicted of such violation shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of § 18.2-11 .
The SFPC shall supersede any fire prevention regulations previously adopted by a local government or other political subdivision.

The fire official may require notification prior to (i) activities involving the handling, storage, or use of substances, materials, or devices regulated by the SFPC; (ii) conducting processes that produce conditions hazardous to life or property; or (iii) establishing a place of assembly.

Operational permits may be required by the fire official as permitted under the SFPC in accordance with Table 107.2, except that the fire official shall require permits for the manufacturing, storage, handling, use, and sale of explosives.
Compressed gas. An operational permit is required for the storage, use, or handling at normal temperature and pressure (NTP) of compressed gases in excess of the amounts listed in this table.
3. Fixed-site hot work equipment such as welding booths.
Industrial ovens. An operational permit is required for operation of industrial ovens regulated by Chapter 30.

Exception: An operational permit is not required for individual containers with a 500-gallon (1893 L) water capacity or less or multiple container systems having an aggregate quantity not exceeding 500 gallons (1893 L), serving occupancies in Group R-3.
Open flames and candles. An operational permit is required to use open flames or candles in connection with assembly areas or dining areas of restaurants or drinking establishments.
Places of assembly. An operational permit is required to operate a place of assembly.
Cutting and welding. An operational permit is required to conduct cutting or welding operations within the jurisdiction.
Application for a permit shall be made on forms prescribed by the fire official.

Before a permit is issued, the fire official shall make such inspections or tests as are necessary to ensure that the use and activities for which application is made comply with the provisions of this code.
Permits shall remain in effect until revoked or for such period as specified on the permit. Permits are not transferable.
Issued permits shall be kept on the premises designated therein at all times and shall be readily available for inspection by the fire official.

The fire official may grant modifications to any provision of the SFPC upon application by the owner or the owner's agent provided the spirit and intent of the SFPC are observed and public health, welfare, and safety are assured.
The appeal shall be submitted to the LBFPCA within 14 calendar days of the application of the SFPC.
The LBFPCA shall meet within 30 calendar days after the date of receipt of the application for appeal.
Application shall be made to the State Review Board within 21 calendar days of receipt of the decision to be appealed.

steps.step: List the studio's regulated activities and quantities
steps.who: You, with your gas supplier and mechanical contractor
steps.how: Write down: each fuel-fired furnace, glory hole, kiln and annealer with its fuel and Btu rating; every torch and bench burner; the oxygen supply (cylinders or a bulk or concentrator system) and the flammable gases (propane, natural gas, acetylene) in cubic feet at normal temperature and pressure; propane storage in gallons; how many people will be in the shop at once for classes, demonstrations and events; whether candles or open flames will be used in a dining or lounge area; and any outdoor tents for events. Albemarle's fee schedule reproduces SFPC Table 107.2 and marks each line 'Yes' where the County requires the permit, so the activities below are the ones to match.
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC § 107.2 and Table 107.2); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: The County's fee schedule follows the Statewide Fire Prevention Code's Table 107.2 line by line.

steps.step: Compressed gas permit: oxygen above 504 cubic feet, flammable gas above 200 cubic feet
steps.how: The compressed gas permit is needed to store, use or handle compressed gases above the table amounts: oxidizing gases including oxygen, 504 cubic feet at NTP; flammable gases (other than cryogenic fluids and LP-gas), 200 cubic feet; inert and simple asphyxiant gases, 6,000 cubic feet; corrosive, 200; highly toxic, toxic and pyrophoric, any amount. Two or three large oxygen cylinders for torch work will cross the 504 cubic foot line, so most torch studios need this permit; a bulk liquid oxygen tank is a cryogenic fluid (10 gallons inside a building, 50 outside) with its own permit line. The County lists the permit as annual per location at $200, with a facility inspection.
steps.deadline: Before the gas is stored or used above the threshold; annual
steps.fee: $200 per year per location, plus the facility inspection fee (first two hours free, then $100 per hour)
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, compressed gas, permit amounts); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule

steps.step: Hot work permit for glory holes, torch benches and public demonstrations
steps.how: SFPC Table 107.2 requires a hot work permit for public exhibitions and demonstrations where hot work is conducted, for portable hot work equipment inside a structure (unless under a construction permit), and for fixed-site hot work equipment such as welding booths. The County's schedule splits the line into a facility permit (annual per location), a fixed-site permit (annual per location) and other hot work (per event, 30 days per location), with $200 and $100 amounts that the scanned table does not align cleanly; ask the Fire Marshal's Office which line a glory hole and torch bench fall under and whether an approved Hot Work Program lets your trained staff issue internal permits. A separate cutting and welding permit ($100 per event per location) covers metalwork such as fabricating tools or stands.
steps.deadline: Before hot work starts; annual for fixed-site equipment
steps.fee: Hot work: $200 (facility or fixed-site, annual per location) or $100 (other, per event) as read from the County schedule; cutting and welding: $100 per event per location
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, hot work operations; cutting and welding); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.quote: 1. Public exhibitions and demonstrations where hot work is conducted.

steps.step: LP-gas permit for any propane storage and use
steps.who: You and your propane supplier; Fire Marshal's Office
steps.how: An operational permit is required for the storage and use of LP-gas; the only exception is containers of 500 gallons water capacity or less serving a Group R-3 home, so a studio's propane tank or cylinder bank needs the permit whatever its size. The County lists it as annual per location at $200 with inspection. The tank itself also needs a mechanical permit from Community Development (above-ground tanks $120; gas lines $40), and in an Entrance Corridor the tank's location and screening are part of the site plan or Certificate of Appropriateness.
steps.deadline: Before propane is delivered and used; annual
steps.fee: $200 per year per location, plus inspection
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, LP-gas); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule; Community Development fee schedule

steps.step: Industrial ovens permit for fuel-fired furnaces and kilns
steps.how: IFC Chapter 30 (industrial ovens) covers fuel-fired and electric ovens and furnaces used in industrial processes, and SFPC Table 107.2 requires an operational permit to operate them. A gas-fired glass melting furnace, glory hole and gas kilns are the kind of equipment this line is written for; electric kilns and annealers may or may not be treated the same way. The County lists the permit as annual per location at $200. Expect the inspection to check the equipment's installation against the building permit, its safety controls and shut-offs, clearances to combustibles, ventilation and fire extinguishers.
steps.fee: $200 per year per location, plus inspection
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, industrial ovens); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.quote: Industrial ovens. An operational permit is required for operation of industrial ovens
steps.paraphrase: Operating an industrial oven needs an operational permit under the County's schedule.

steps.step: Places of assembly permit if more than 50 people gather; open flames and candles if a dining area uses them
steps.how: The County requires an operational permit to operate a place of assembly with more than 50 persons (annual per location, $200). If classes, demonstrations, openings or sip-and-blow events bring more than 50 people into the studio or an event room, get this permit and make sure the building permit and certificate of occupancy allow the assembly use and occupant load. Candles or open flames in a dining or drinking area need the open flames and candles permit ($200 a year if it is your only permit, $100 if ancillary to another), and the Fire Marshal publishes code compliance guidelines for open-flame decorative devices (no Class I or II liquids or LP-gas, self-extinguishing devices, enclosed flames, chimneys and shades of noncombustible materials).
steps.deadline: Before the first gathering of more than 50 people; annual
steps.fee: Places of assembly: $200 per year per location; open flames and candles: $200 (annual if sole permit) or $100 (if ancillary to another permit)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026); Fire Marshal fee schedule; Open-Flame Decorative Devices Code Compliance Guidelines (PDF, Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A place of assembly for more than 50 people needs an operational permit.
steps.quote: An operational permit is required to operate a place of assembly (greater than 50 persons).

steps.step: Apply on the Fire Prevention Permit Application (General) form
steps.who: You; Fire Rescue Community Risk & Resilience
steps.how: Use the County's online Fire Prevention Permit Application – General (the Permits & Inspections page links it; the tent and blasting applications are separate forms). Give the business and property details, the permit types, the gases and quantities, equipment and occupant loads. For questions, email the section's group mailbox or call Fire Rescue through the County switchboard. Fees are paid by credit card through Fire Rescue's Permits & Inspection Payments link.
steps.deadline: Before the activity; the Fire Marshal inspects before issuing
steps.fee: Per permit (see fees); paid online by credit card
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC § 107.3); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page and Payments page (Internet Archive copy of 13 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: Fire Rescue takes credit card payments online for permits and inspections among other services.

steps.step: Pass the facility inspection; fix violations before the re-inspection
steps.how: The fire official inspects before issuing the permit. The County's facility inspection fee for any fixed facility requiring a Table 107.2 permit is no charge for the first two hours and $100 an hour after that. If violations are found and corrected, the re-inspection is free; if not, each further re-inspection is $100 until the violations are corrected or a remediation agreement is reached. After the initial inspection, annual inspections fall due by the inspection anniversary date. Keep every issued permit on the premises, available to the fire official.
steps.deadline: Annual inspections due by the inspection anniversary date
steps.fee: Facility inspection: first two hours no charge, $100 per hour thereafter; re-inspection: $0 if violations corrected, $100 per inspection if not
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC §§ 107.4, 107.8); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026); Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: If violations found at the first inspection are not fixed, every re-inspection is charged until they are fixed or a remediation agreement is reached.

steps.step: For outdoor events: tent permit, and the lead-time pricing
steps.who: You or the event organizer; Fire Marshal's Office
steps.how: A tent or air-supported structure over 900 square feet, or with more than 50 occupants, needs a tent permit (per event, good for 30 days per location, renewable up to five times for 180 days in 12 months). The fee depends on how early you apply: $100 if the application is received 30 days before the event, $150 at 15 to 29 days, $200 at 8 to 15 days, $300 at 7 days or less. Use the Fire Prevention Permit Application – Tent form and the County's tent requirements sheet. Food trucks at your events need a current fire inspection from their home jurisdiction (no County fee for food truck inspections).
steps.deadline: Apply at least 30 days before the event for the lowest fee
steps.fee: Tent permit: $100 (30 days before), $150 (15 to 29 days), $200 (8 to 15 days), $300 (7 days or less)
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2, temporary membrane structures and tents); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page
steps.paraphrase: A tent permit runs 30 days and can be renewed five times, for at most 180 days in a year.

steps.step: If a code provision does not fit your equipment: ask the fire official for a modification
steps.who: You or your engineer; the fire official
steps.how: The fire official may grant a modification of any SFPC provision on written application where the spirit and intent of the code are kept and safety is assured; you must supply technical data, and the official may ask for an engineer's statement. The decision is written and recorded. The County's schedule lists a Request for Fire Code Variance/Modification fee ($50 per application as read from the table).
steps.fee: Request for Fire Code Variance/Modification: $50 per application (as read from the fee table)
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-60 (SFPC §§ 106.5, 106.5.1, 106.5.2); Albemarle County Fire Marshal fee schedule
steps.quote: The application for modification and the final decision of the fire official shall be in writing and shall be recorded in the permanent records of the local enforcing agency.

caveats: www.albemarle.org refuses automated readers; the Fire Rescue pages and the fee schedule PDF are Internet Archive copies (dates in the sources), and County quotes carry paraphrases because the County's terms bar reposting.

The Fire Marshal fee schedule is a scanned table whose permit, fee and inspection columns do not line up in extracted text. The $200 annual figure for compressed gas, LP-gas, industrial ovens and places of assembly, the $100 and $200 hot work figures, the $100 cutting and welding fee, and the miscellaneous fees ($100 plan review per set of plans, $50 modification request, $350 Board of Appeals application, $100 re-inspection) follow the PDF's reading order and the County web page where it repeats them; confirm each with the Fire Marshal's Office before budgeting.

SFPC Table 107.2 is 'to be filled in by local jurisdiction': the County's schedule marks which permits Albemarle requires. Whether a glass furnace and glory hole are 'industrial ovens', 'hot work', both, or something else is the fire official's call; the County pages do not mention glass studios.

The 2021 Statewide Fire Prevention Code (13VAC5-52) took effect January 18, 2024, replacing 13VAC5-51; the County's 2022 fee schedule cites Table 107.2 of the earlier edition, whose permit lines match the ones quoted here.

No direct telephone number for the Fire Marshal's Office was found on the pages read; the County switchboard is listed. The group mailbox printed on the permits page contains an ampersand and its link is empty, so it may be mistyped on the page.
The Fire Prevention Permit Application web forms were not opened (the archived copies show only a captcha shell); their fields are not described.
